source.title: GloNets: Globally Connected Neural Networks
source.authors: Antonio Di Cecco; C. Metta; Marco Fantozzi; F. Morandin; Maurizio Parton

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper; no material truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training and depth behavior of GloNet and ResNet variants using learning curves, test error, and accuracy, which bears on V3's claim about depth-related degradation and shortcuts. Its architecture and tasks differ from the specified original results.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-curve shape, test errors, and accuracy, not training classification error. Keep results that directly measure training dynamics or depth-related performance; cited results about other papers are not rows. CIFAR-10 results do not state training error.
record.test_reason: The study uses established depth-degradation and shortcut findings to motivate GloNet and evaluates architecture performance. Its depth sweeps report regression test MSE and MNIST accuracy, rather than the convolutional training-error comparison in V3. Its batch-normalization ablations report regression test error, rather than accuracy gain or learning-rate tolerance in V6. None of its results tests a supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: GloNet maintains performance across tested depths and achieves comparable outcomes in roughly half the ResNet training time where ResNet is stable. These are the authors' architecture-performance conclusions, not demonstrations of the supplied training-error claims.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates a globally connected architecture against ResNetv2 and other baselines; uses regression, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ViT settings rather than the original recipes named in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with architecture and task: ResNetv2 degrades at high depth on SGEMM and MNIST; GloNet is described as depth-consistent. CIFAR-10 ResNet20/GloNet test errors are nearly equal. ViT/GloNet-ViT differences vary by encoder count.

fits_no_version.finding: GloNet maintains similar regression test curves across depth, while ResNetv2 test MSE rises to 0.040 and 0.048 at nominal depths 600 and 1000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global connections can preserve test performance across depth in fully connected SGEMM regression.

fits_no_version.finding: GloNet MNIST accuracy remains consistent across depth, while vanilla and ResNetv2 accuracy declines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global connections can preserve fully connected MNIST classification accuracy across depth.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet20 and GloNet have overlapping CIFAR-10 learning curves; GloNet-ViT has similar or somewhat higher best accuracy than ViT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GloNet can match or improve the evaluated architectures' CIFAR-10 predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: SGEMM ResNetv2 without batch normalization has higher test MSE than its normalized counterpart, especially at greater depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization improves test performance of the evaluated fully connected residual regression networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Symposium on Intelligent Data Analysis (2023)
record.problems: The directly relevant depth comparisons report regression test error and learning-curve shape or MNIST accuracy, rather than training classification error. Most depth results are figures, with no uncertainty estimates stated. CIFAR-10 comparisons report test accuracy/error but not training error.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying additional results left out. Figure-only exact accuracies for the MNIST depth sweep were not transcribed because the text provides no exact values.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, training duration, and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.

Depth-dependent training classification error in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks; longer-training controls; special tanh initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Initialization comparisons measuring training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization in matched networks, and comparable training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V3 limits_scope labels should be removed: different outcome measures and untested parts do not establish scope limitations. Figure captions explicitly identify the SGEMM learning curves as test-error curves.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam from random initialization, model size and training-duration conditions.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU experiments, spurious minima, and width comparisons.

Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks with and without identity shortcuts on ImageNet or CIFAR-10 as specified; the study uses different architectures and includes fully connected MNIST and SGEMM tasks, plus a CIFAR-10 ResNet20/GloNet comparison.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth under those initializations.
Learning-rate stability threshold, curvature or sharpness behavior, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance in the named settings, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: GloNet
rows.size_stated: Fully connected; 16 units per block; 10, 24, 50, 100, 200, 600, or 1000 blocks
rows.operation_detail: Trained at varying depths on SGEMM GPU kernel regression; learning-curve shape reported as consistent across depths.
rows.value: Learning curve maintained its shape across the tested depths.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes the training curves as unaffected by increasing depth.
rows.check: Figures 2–3 plot test MSE during training, not training loss or training classification error. GloNet's stable test curves do not establish V3.

rows.subject: ResNetv2 baseline
rows.size_stated: Fully connected; 16 units per block; equivalent depths 10, 24, 50, 100, 200, 600, or 1000 blocks
rows.operation_detail: Trained at varying depths on SGEMM GPU kernel regression; learning-curve shape and best test error reported.
rows.measure: Training learning-curve shape and best test error
rows.baseline: GloNet learning curve maintains its shape; best test error around 0.02 across depths.
rows.value: ResNet learning curve became flatter as depth increased; best test error increased to 0.04 and almost 0.05 at 600 and 1000 blocks, respectively.
rows.note: The reported depth degradation is in the training-curve shape and test error, not training classification error.
rows.check: The curves measure test MSE in fully connected regression. Table 2 gives ResNetv2 errors of 0.040 and 0.048 at nominal depths 600 and 1000. Depth labels are halved for actual ResNetv2 block counts; the record incorrectly presents them as equivalent actual block counts.

source_check.correct: Depths 10, 24, 50, 100, 200, 600, 1000 are nominal comparison depths; actual ResNetv2 block counts are 5, 12, 25, 50, 100, 300, 500. ResNetv2 best test MSE is 0.040 and 0.048 at nominal depths 600 and 1000; corresponding GloNet values are both 0.022.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.size_stated: ResNet20; 3 stages of 3 residual blocks each
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs; learning curves compared with its GloNet version.
rows.measure: Best test error and learning curves
rows.value: 91.12% best test error; learning curves completely overlapping.
rows.note: This reports test error rather than training error, so it cannot establish the training-error claim in V3.
rows.check: A single-depth ResNet20–GloNet comparison cannot establish depth degradation or its prevention. The paper calls 91.12% and 91.08% test errors, but these percentages appear to be accuracies; the supplied text cannot resolve that reporting inconsistency.

relation.reason: Depth sweeps report fully connected regression test MSE or MNIST accuracy; CIFAR-10 convolutional results compare architectures at one depth. These do not test V3's training-error effect, and normalization comparisons do not establish V6's faster accuracy gains or higher learning-rate tolerance.

tranche.reason: Uses depth-degradation, shortcut and normalization findings to develop GloNet; reports its architecture's performance without measuring the effects specified by the supplied claim versions.

source_check.notes: SGEMM learning curves measure test MSE; MNIST accuracy is not identified as training accuracy. The source calls the CIFAR-10 values 91.12% and 91.08% test errors; interpreting them as accuracies remains unconfirmed.
